associations.rationale: This constructs an opaque ClassIndex-indexed family of D4 representations but makes no classification or indecomposability claim by itself.
Indecomposability of each canonical representative is one ingredient in the twelve-object classification, but it does not state completeness or distinctness.
Pairwise nonisomorphism of the canonical family is another ingredient in counting the twelve indecomposables, not the full source classification on its own.
The cardinality twelve concerns the auxiliary ClassIndex; only together with the family properties does it yield the source's count of indecomposable objects.

This gives each indecomposable a unique index in the canonical family, but the cardinality of `ClassIndex` and indecomposability of every canonical representation are separate facts; by itself it does not state that there are exactly twelve indecomposable classes.

Membership of an indecomposable's dimension vector in a fixed list is a necessary numerical consequence of the classification, but it does not identify the representation or establish the twelve isomorphism classes.
